decision.what_is_decided: Whether optional caller rules are a valid config and can be compiled into regexes, versus rejected.

inputs.name: rules
inputs.source: JevOptions.rules passed into createJevLogs then compileRules
inputs.role: Candidate list of match/route objects to validate and compile

outcomes: list of named compiled regex-plus-route objects
decision.downstream_action: createJevLogs stores the list and later tests redacted log bodies against it before any model call.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Branches only check undefined, Array, length cap, object shape, route enum, name length, match type, flag charset, and RegExp syntax.

context_dependence.evidence: Each rule is validated in isolation with no log body, severity, or runtime telemetry context.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: The contract is a closed schema: types, numeric caps, allowed flag letters, and whether new RegExp succeeds.

judgment_required.evidence: Invalid input always throws; valid input always compiles. No competing interpretations of meaning.

rule_stability.evidence: Limits and allowed fields are fixed library invariants, not evolving operational policy about logs.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Caps on rule count and pattern length are resource/safety bounds, not incident-severity policy.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: No free-form log text is read; match strings are treated only as regex source, not as language to interpret.

decision_complexity.evidence: A short guard chain plus per-item field checks; no competing outcomes about what a log means.

observed.claim: Undefined rules become an empty compiled list without further work.

evidence.observation: The function returns an empty array when the rules argument is undefined.

observed.claim: Non-array input or too many rules is rejected with RangeError.

evidence.observation: A type and length check throws before any compilation.

observed.claim: Each rule is compiled only after exact field checks, or the function throws.

evidence.observation: The map validates object shape, route, name, match, and flags, then builds a RegExp or throws.

inferred.claim: This stayed deterministic because it is a construction-time schema compiler for later exact matches, not triage of log meaning.

evidence.observation: createJevLogs calls compileRules once while building the triage closure.
Compiled regexes are applied with first-match-wins before cache or evaluator, as exact shortcuts.

unknown: Whether the author ever considered Jev for config validation.
What rule patterns real callers actually supply.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: The Jev site interprets leftover log text; compileRules never reads a log body.

evidence.observation: jevEvaluator sends state into questions about urgency, diagnostic value, and investigation worth.
compileRules only inspects the rules array structure and regex syntax.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Outcomes are accept/reject/compile of config, not priority, value, or retain versus analyze of a log.

evidence.observation: Jev questions choose among urgency labels and a diagnostic score.
This function returns [] , throws, or emits compiled regex objects.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: It runs at setup, not per log.

evidence.observation: Compilation happens inside createJevLogs, not inside triage.

decision.what_is_decided: Whether one rule object is well-formed and which compiled regex and route to emit for it.

inputs.name: rule
inputs.source: One element of the rules array inside compileRules
inputs.role: Object whose route, name, match, and flags must satisfy the schema

inputs.name: index
inputs.role: Used only to label errors and default the rule name

outcomes: compiled named regex with retain or analyze route
decision.downstream_action: The compiled regex is later tested against redacted body text; first hit short-circuits Jev.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Route must be one of two literals; flags must be a subset of a four-letter charset; match must compile as RegExp.

context_dependence.evidence: Validation uses only the rule object and its index, not the log or surrounding pipeline state.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Membership in a tiny alphabet, length caps, instanceof, and RegExp constructor success fully specify the result.

judgment_required.evidence: No interpretation of what the pattern is meant to catch; only whether it is a legal regex and route.

rule_stability.evidence: Allowed flags and field limits are a stable API contract.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Does not classify incidents or choose retain versus analyze for a log; it only accepts caller-chosen routes.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: The flags charset test is a character-class membership check, not reading operational prose.

decision_complexity.evidence: A handful of type and format gates, then construct or throw.

observed.claim: A pre-built RegExp is copied with global/sticky flags stripped; a string match is compiled with caller flags.

evidence.observation: Two arms construct a RegExp from either an existing pattern source or a string plus flags.

observed.claim: Flags are accepted only if they match a tiny allowed-letter pattern; otherwise throw.

evidence.observation: flags is type-checked and tested against a closed letter set before new RegExp.

observed.claim: Invalid regex syntax becomes a RangeError, not a classification.

evidence.observation: A try/catch around the constructor rethrows as RangeError with the rule index.

inferred.claim: Deterministic because the library must fail fast on illegal config rather than guess what the caller meant.

evidence.observation: The comment and signature describe validate-and-compile that throws on the first invalid rule.

unknown: Why callers would pass string versus RegExp match forms.
Whether anyone considered a model to repair or interpret bad rules.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Jev classifies untrusted log prose; this callback only checks that a config pattern is a legal regex.

evidence.observation: Jev instructions treat the log as untrusted data and ask about investigation worth and urgency.
Here match is only source text for RegExp, and flags are a charset check.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: The static text test is against allowed regex flag letters, not against log content.

evidence.observation: The pattern test is applied to the flags string of the rule, not to a log body.

decision.what_is_decided: After triage, whether this OpenTelemetry record is forwarded to the wrapped exporter or omitted from the batch.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.role: Selects annotate-all versus drop retained records

inputs.name: decision.route
inputs.source: Result of this.jev.triage for the record
inputs.role: Already-chosen retain versus analyze used as a keep/drop bit

inputs.name: record
inputs.source: Current ReadableLogRecord in the export batch
inputs.role: Payload to copy and annotate if kept

outcomes: keep a cloned record with jev attributes merged
decision.downstream_action: Kept records are forwarded to the inner exporter; an empty keep-list still succeeds the callback.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Keep versus skip is equality on a two-value mode and a two-value route already produced by triage.

context_dependence.evidence: Depends only on configured exporter mode plus the triage route, not on re-reading the log body.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: A single conjunction of two closed enumerations fully specifies omit versus keep.

judgment_required.evidence: No new interpretation of the log; the semantic work is delegated to triage before this branch.

rule_stability.evidence: Mode and route vocabularies are fixed in the public types and comments.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: analysis-only is a pipeline split so a later LLM branch sees only analyze-routed records, not a new risk judgment.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: The compared tokens are option and enum identifiers, not free-form log language.

decision_complexity.evidence: One keep-or-skip gate after an already-completed triage call.

observed.claim: Each worker calls triage first, then optionally skips when mode is analysis-only and route is retain.

evidence.observation: triage runs, then a conjunction of mode and route continues without writing output.

observed.claim: Otherwise the record is cloned and jev attributes are merged in.

evidence.observation: output at that index becomes a shallow copy of record fields plus decisionAttributes.

observed.claim: Mode is a closed exporter option documented as annotate versus a separate analysis branch.

evidence.observation: The option comment states annotate keeps every record and analysis-only is only for a separate LLM branch.

inferred.claim: This stayed an exact filter because the semantic retain/analyze judgment is already finished in triage; the exporter only applies a deployment mode to that bit.

evidence.observation: The skip uses decision.route from triage rather than inspecting body or severity again.
Route itself is computed earlier from Jev scores, threshold, and priority inside triage.

unknown: Why a given deployment chooses annotate versus analysis-only.
Whether the author considered a second Jev pass at export time.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: The Jev site produces priority, value, and investigation worth from log text; this callback consumes an already-made route.

evidence.observation: jevEvaluator asks choice/score/boolean questions over state.
The non-Jev branch only compares mode and decision.route.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: Keep versus drop is a closed equality, not competing semantic labels.

evidence.observation: Jev priority has four urgency criteria over untrusted log prose.
Here omit happens only for one mode and one route pair.

differences_from_jev_site.claim: This function still invokes triage, so Jev may run earlier in the same callback; the contrast gate itself does not.

evidence.observation: triage is awaited per record before the mode filter.
